correctness.rationale: The one-probe FlexTrace definition yields T=(omega^T A omega)^2/[omega^T(A^2+zeta A)omega] exactly. For a diagonal two-eigenvalue A the independent chi-square radial factor and exact rational-angle integrals give E T=[a^2(1+2t/s)+2ab+b^2(1+2s/t)]/(s+t)^2. Subtracting a^2/s^2+b^2/t^2 factors to [(a t/s)-(b s/t)]^2/(s+t)^2 and hence the claimed ab(a-b)^2 formula. The sharp fraction comparison follows by s+t>s; limits follow by positive-variable continuity and the exact ratio. 84 exact-rational identities, 756 literal matrix evaluations, 8 independent angular quadratures and 15 matched-scale checks succeeded. Neither finite tests nor numerical logs are used as infinite proofs. No assertion is made at regularization exactly zero.

originality.rationale: The March 2026 FlexTrace source defines the estimator but gives general bounds rather than an exact one-probe nonlinear effective-dimension bias. Its explicit spectral-tail bias bound requires at least four probes; the current one-probe expectation and nonuniform matched-scale limit are not entailed. Earlier funNyström traces the matrix function of a sketch rather than reusing its Gaussian probe; XNysTrace unbiasedness pertains to linear matrix traces. Relevant full-text primary comparisons and published searches revealed no covering statement. Older Gaussian quadratic-form literature could contain equivalent algebra, and the check is not an independence or uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: A general older calculation of the expectation of a ratio of Gaussian quadratic forms might algebraically imply the two-eigenvalue identity, even if it does not mention FlexTrace.
Published-index semantic searches and three primary-source inspections cannot establish unique priority across all literature.
The theorem is specific to a minimal one-probe 2x2 setting and does not establish the same boundary for practical larger sketch budgets.

value.rationale: Effective dimension tr[A(A+zeta I)^{-1}] is a naturally regularized invariant relevant to kernel learning. The theorem gives a complete exact bias classification on a natural minimal spectral family, a sharp relative-loss envelope, and a joint singular-scale law: when zeta/gap is held fixed as the small eigenvalue tends to zero, the estimator misses the full O(1) contribution of that vanishing mode. Its two iterated limits differ by one, a nontrivial nonuniformity that is not a mere negative type check or a random finite-parameter recomputation. It can inform effective-dimension benchmark design and interpretation of one-pass sketch guarantees without implying a general algorithmic impossibility.
